question: Find the latest MX1 Bill of Materials and summarize what it covers.
answer:
Here is a comprehensive summary of all three latest MX1 Bills of Materials:

---

## MX1 Bill of Materials — Summary

There are **three active BOM documents** covering the MX1 Portable X-ray System, each serving a distinct scope:

---

### 1. BOM-055 Rev G — MX1 Top-Level Assembly
<cite>BOM-055 Rev G</cite>

This is the **highest-level hardware BOM**, defining what ships to the customer as the complete MX1 product. It covers:

| Line Item | Description | Qty |
|---|---|---|
| **E1** (BOM-004, Rev K) | Emitter | 1 |
| **C1** (BOM-008, Rev L) | Cassette | 1 |
| **H1** (BOM-019, Rev D) | Wired Charger | 2 |
| **P1** (BOM-037, Rev G) | Pelican Case | 1 |
| **M10637 Rev B** | Physical IFU-MX1 Booklet | 1 |
| **M11177 Rev A** | Physical Emergency Instructions Booklet | 1 |
| **MS-10627** (BOM-056, Rev F) | Puck Box with Pucks | 1 |
| **MS-10334** (Overshipper Assembly) | MX1 Cardboard Overshipper + Labels + GTIN + UN 3481 Label | 1 |
| **M50703** | Packaging Tape | 1 |

Rev G (via ECR-593) updated the Emitter to BOM Rev K, Cassette to BOM Rev L, Pelican Case to BOM Rev G, Puck Box to BOM Rev F, and updated the overshipper label to Rev C.

---

### 2. BOM-079 Rev P — MX1 Software System v3.4.0
<cite>BOM-079 Rev P</cite>

This is the **detailed hardware/component-level BOM** for the MX1 system built on software version 3.4.0. It is organized into multiple assembly sections:

- **ASM-100 — Imager Emitter:** Hundreds of components including the 60 kV X-ray tube (Micro X-Ray), emitter main PCB, display PCB, laser PCB, LIDAR PCB, infrared & visible cameras, collimator, aluminum filter disk, beam-limiting pucks (6 sizes: 20.0, 26.3, 32.5, 38.8, 45.0 cm SID, and 5×5), enclosure halfshells, gaskets, harnesses, and decals.
- **ASM-200 — Imager Control Unit:** Includes the high-voltage power supply (Spellman 65 kV), Intel NUC computer, 16 GB RAM, 256 GB SSD, Wi-Fi adapter/antenna, power manager PCBs, NEMA enclosure, fans, cables, and a full suite of connectors and fasteners.
- **ASM-300 — Cassette Assembly** and additional cable/puck assemblies are also covered.
- A **software BOM (SBOM) sheet** is included covering the software stack.

---

### 3. BOM-101 Rev A — MX1 Software System v4.0.1
<cite>BOM-101 Rev A</cite>

This is the **most current detailed component-level BOM**, tied to software version **v4.0.1** (the successor to v3.4.0 in BOM-079). It shares the same assembly structure (ASM-100, ASM-200, ASM-300, cables, pucks, SBOM) and appears to have largely the same hardware content as BOM-079 Rev P, updated to reflect the new software version. This is the latest and most current snapshot of the full MX1 component set.

---

### How They Relate

| Document | Scope | Latest Rev |
|---|---|---|
| **BOM-055** | Shipped product (top-level, customer-facing) | Rev G |
| **BOM-079** | Full hardware + software component detail (SW v3.4.0) | Rev P |
| **BOM-101** | Full hardware + software component detail (SW v4.0.1) | Rev A |

In short, **BOM-055 Rev G** defines *what goes in the box*, while **BOM-101 Rev A** is the most current engineering-level component manifest for the entire MX1 system at the latest software version.

question: Does the corpus contain a 510(k) summary for the device?
answer:
No, the corpus does not contain a standalone 510(k) summary document. After a full inventory of all 188 documents across 165 unique IDs — covering types such as PLN, MEMO, RSK, VVPR, BOM, ECR, DHF, DMR, ESF, IFU, QSR, TRA, and 3P — there is no document with a title like "510(k) Summary," "510(k) Premarket Notification," or similar regulatory submission document.

The corpus does, however, contain **references to** MedAI's 510(k) activity:

- <cite>PLN-P01-060 Rev C</cite> mentions that MedAI submitted a 510(k) (K231372) to the FDA in April 2023, and that on February 6, 2024, the FDA issued a "not substantially equivalent" (NSE) letter. The reference list also cites "FDA 510(K) K231372, MX1 Portable X-ray System" as an external reference.
- <cite>MEMO-P01-699 Rev A OBSOLETE</cite> references FDA 510(k) guidance documents in the context of evaluating design changes.
- <cite>PLN-P01-061</cite> (the MX1 Regulatory Plan) may contain further detail on the 510(k) strategy, but is not itself a 510(k) summary.

In short, the 510(k) submission (K231372) itself — including any formal 510(k) Summary document — does not appear to be stored in this QMS corpus. It would be an external FDA submission document rather than an internal QMS record.

question: What verification protocols exist for electrical safety?
answer:
This is very comprehensive. I now have a complete picture of the electrical safety verification landscape. Let me compile the full answer.

Here is a comprehensive overview of all the electrical safety verification protocols for the MX1 Portable X-ray System:

---

## Electrical Safety Verification Protocols — MX1 Portable X-ray System

The electrical safety verification program spans **third-party lab testing**, **in-house protocol-driven testing**, and **software-level safety monitoring**, all governed by the IEC 60601 family of standards.

---

### 1. IEC 60601-1 General Electrical Safety (Third-Party — Intertek, Rev E)

The foundational electrical safety evaluation was conducted by **Intertek Testing Services** at their Springfield, Illinois facility. The scope covered basic safety and essential performance per **IEC 60601-1:2005 Ed.3+A2:2020**.

> Testing used n=1 DV unit (E1 Emitter, C1 Cassette, F1 Foot Pedal, T1 Tablet, SW v3.0.0-delta). Type tests per IEC 60601-1 Section 5.2. Result: **PASS**. <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite> <cite>PLN-P01-065 Rev C</cite>

The same Intertek report (**3P-P01-28**) simultaneously covered multiple collateral and particular standards:

| Standard | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| IEC 60601-1 Ed. 3.2 | General electrical safety & essential performance | PASS |
| IEC 60601-1-3 Ed. 2.2 | Radiation protection collateral standard | PASS |
| IEC 60601-1-6 Ed. 3.2 | Usability collateral standard | PASS (document review) |
| IEC 60601-2-28 Ed. 3.0 | X-ray tube assemblies basic safety | PASS |
| IEC 60601-2-43 Ed. 3 | X-ray equipment for interventional procedures | PASS |
| IEC 60601-2-54 Ed. 2.0 | X-ray equipment for radiography & radioscopy | PASS |

<cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>

---

### 2. Dielectric and Leakage Testing (Third-Party — Intertek, Rev F)

A dedicated re-evaluation was triggered for **MX1 Rev F** because a design change was made to the power isolation component (isolated DC/DC converter for the 5V rail on the USB port region) in the **C1 Cassette Main PCBA**.

**Document:** <cite>3P-P01-33 Rev A</cite> — *Intertek IEC 60601-1 MX1 Rev F Dielectric and Leakage Summary Report*

- **Scope:** Dielectric (hipot) and leakage current performance per **IEC 60601-1:2005 Ed.3+A1+A2**
- **System tested:** E1 Emitter (SN1281/DV27), C1 Cassette (SN1280/DV27), H1 Wired Charger (Lot 10146, Qty 2), F1 Foot Pedal, K1 Cart, T1 Tablet, Collimation Pucks; SW v4.0.0-alpha
- **Special equipment:** USB-C cable with shorted conductors to comply with IEC 60601-1 Section 8.8.3
- **Result:** **PASS** — all dielectric and leakage safety evaluations passed per IEC 60601-1

<cite>3P-P01-33 Rev A</cite>

---

### 3. W1 Wireless Charger — Foreign Object Detection (FOD) & Resonance Lock

Because the W1 Wireless Charger poses an electrical burn hazard by potentially transmitting energy into unintended metal objects, a dedicated in-house protocol was created and executed.

**Document:** <cite>VVPR-P01-148 Rev C</cite> — *WTX Foreign Object Detection and Resonance Lock Verification Protocol and Report*

- **Standards referenced:** IEC 60601-1 Ed. 3.1 Clause 4.2.3.2; **IEC 62368-1 Ed. 4.0 Clause 9.6.3**
- **Responsible department:** Electrical Engineering (MedAI)
- **Sample size:** n=1 (type test per IEC 60601-1:2005 Clause 5.2)
- **Test objects (per IEC 62368-1):** Steel disc, Aluminum ring, Aluminum foil
- **What was measured:** Foreign object temperature, TX coil temperature, LED state, and input power during and after object placement

**Acceptance criteria and results (all PASS):**

| Foreign Object | Max Allowed FO Temp | Actual FO Temp Range | TX Temp Limit | Input Power Limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Steel Disc | 85°C | 35–40°C | 104°C | <5 W (actual: 2.5 W) |
| Aluminum Ring | 120°C | 33–36°C | 104°C | <5 W (actual: 2.5 W) |
| Aluminum Foil | 155°C | 38–43°C | 104°C | <5 W (actual: 2.5 W) |

Additionally, when the W1 detects a foreign object, its LED state must turn **RED** (confirmed PASS for all tests). The IFU warning against placing metals near the charger was also verified (IFU Section 4). <cite>VVPR-P01-148 Rev C</cite>

---

### 4. Software-Level Electrical Safety Monitoring (In-House)

Two software verification protocols address real-time electrical safety monitoring within the MX1 system:

#### a) Critical Faults — Temperature & Voltage
**Document:** <cite>VVPR-P01-181 Rev B</cite> — *MX1 Software System Critical Faults v3.1.0*
- Verifies software detection of **temperature faults** on the emitter main PCB, monoblock LV PCB, collimator PCB, and cassette main PCB
- Verifies **voltage monitor fault** detection and entry into a safe state

#### b) Voltage and Temperature Monitoring Accuracy
**Document:** <cite>VVPR-P01-182 Rev B</cite> — *MX1 Software System Voltage and Temperature Monitoring Accuracy v3.1.0*
- Verifies accuracy of voltage and temperature sensors used for fault monitoring
- All monitoring tests passed with accuracies within 10%

<cite>VVPR-P01-181 Rev B</cite> <cite>VVPR-P01-182 Rev B</cite>

---

### 5. Battery Electrical Safety (Third-Party)

Battery packs (Emitter: MS-10010; Cassette: MS-10083) were tested for electrical safety under:
- **UN 38.3** (altitude, thermal, vibration, shock, external short circuit, overcharge)
- **IEC 62133-2** (external short circuit, free fall, overcharge, vibration, mechanical shock)

Result: **PASS** for both standards. <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>

---

### 6. Overarching Governance

- The **V&V Plan** (<cite>PLN-P01-065 Rev C</cite>) governs which electrical safety tests are required per device revision, assigns testing to Intertek or SGS, and specifies that an "Engineering Mode" was developed to allow remote device operation during electrical safety testing.
- The **V&V Summary** (<cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>) confirms all electrical safety testing (Rev E and Rev F) achieved a PASS result.
- The **V&V Trace Matrix** (<cite>VVAM-P01-004 Rev D</cite>) provides requirement-by-requirement traceability linking standards compliance back to test evidence.

---

### Summary Table

| Protocol / Report | Type | Standard(s) | Performer | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3P-P01-28 | 3rd Party | IEC 60601-1, -1-3, -1-6, -2-28, -2-43, -2-54 (Rev E) | Intertek | PASS |
| 3P-P01-33 | 3rd Party | IEC 60601-1 Dielectric & Leakage (Rev F) | Intertek | PASS |
| VVPR-P01-148 Rev C | In-house | IEC 60601-1 Cl. 4.2.3.2; IEC 62368-1 Cl. 9.6.3 (FOD) | MedAI EE Dept. | PASS |
| VVPR-P01-181 Rev B | In-house | Software critical fault detection | MedAI | PASS |
| VVPR-P01-182 Rev B | In-house | Software voltage/temp monitoring accuracy | MedAI | PASS |
| 3P-P01-25 | 3rd Party | UN 38.3 / IEC 62133-2 battery safety | Energy Assurance | PASS |

question: Trace electrical-leakage risk from the risk records to verification evidence.
answer:
I now have a comprehensive picture of the entire electrical-leakage risk trace chain. Let me compile the full analysis.

---

## Electrical-Leakage Risk Trace: Risk Records → Verification Evidence

Here is a full end-to-end traceability map for the MX1 electrical-leakage risk, following the chain from hazard identification → risk scoring → design controls → design requirements → verification testing → test results.

---

## 1. Hazard Identification & Severity Framework

The MX1 Risk Assessment establishes the severity scoring anchor for all electrical hazards:

> **Death (Severity 14)** — "Death of Operator/Patient directly due to the device (i.e., Severe electric shock, explosion)"

<cite>RSK-P01-010 Rev E</cite>

The risk management program is governed by ISO 14971:2019, with IEC 60601-1 as the primary applicable electrical safety standard, and the Risk Management Summary Report confirms: *"The risk management file has been reviewed to demonstrate compliance to IEC 60601-1."* <cite>RSK-P01-017 Rev B</cite>

---

## 2. Risk Records — Electrical Leakage / Shock Hazard Entries

### 2A. Hazard Analysis (RSK-P01-010)

The hazard analysis in RSK-P01-010 contains multiple electrical shock risk entries. The primary mitigation for all of them is **PRD20.5** — full compliance with IEC 60601-1 — backed by design controls including peripheral isolation, insulating enclosure materials, and electrical protection components.

| Risk ID | Hazard Category | Causing Event | Hazardous Situation | Potential Harm | Pre-Mitig. RPN | Mitigation / Control | Req ID | Post-Mitig. RPN |
|---------|----------------|---------------|----------------------|-----------------|----------------|----------------------|--------|-----------------|
| R0057 | Loss of Function / Electrical | Non-approved USB-C cord connected | Excess voltage overcomes peripheral isolation | Shorts circuitry; device inoperable | 4×4 = 16 | **Include Peripheral Isolation** | PRD20.5 | 2×4 = 8 ✅ |
| R0059 | Loss of Function / Electrical | Non-approved USB-C cord + over-voltage | Battery overvoltage | Battery explosion / equipment damage | 2×3 = 6 | Over-voltage protection; **MOVs on USB Lines** | RSK_R118, RSK_R361 | 2×2 = 4 ✅ |
| R0060 | Loss of Function / Electrical | Power surge on MAINS during charging | Large voltage overcomes electrical insulation | Shorts circuitry; device inoperable | 3×4 = 12 | Power supply per IEC 60601-1; **Surge Protection per IEC 60601-1-2 §8.9** | PRD20.5, PRD20.6 | 2×4 = 8 ✅ |
| R0062 | Loss of Function / Electrical | Charger connected to incorrectly-rated outlet | Voltage overcomes electrical insulation | Shorts circuitry; device inoperable | 2×3 = 6 | Power supply per IEC 60601-1; Surge Protection per IEC 60601-1-2 | PRD20.5, PRD20.6 | 2×3 = 6 ✅ |

<cite>RSK-P01-010 Rev E</cite>

### 2B. DFMEA — Component-Level Electrical Shock Entries (RSK-P01-012)

The DFMEA captures electrical shock risks at the component (BOM) level across the Emitter enclosure sub-assemblies. Representative entries:

| DRSK ID | Subassy | Part | Failure Mode | Patient Effect | S×O Pre | Control | S×O Post |
|---------|---------|------|--------------|----------------|---------|---------|---------|
| DRSK0042 | E1 Emitter | MS-10132 Front Face ASSY | Enclosure damaged (large) — mechanical damage exposes internals | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×3 = 12 | Compliance to IEC 60601-1 / **PRD20.5** | 4×3 = 12 ✅ |
| DRSK0045 | E1 Emitter | MS-10132 Front Face ASSY | Fails to maintain clearances — improper specs | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×2 = 8 | Compliance to IEC 60601-1 / **PRD20.5** | 4×2 = 8 ✅ |
| DRSK0046 | E1 Emitter | MS-10132 Front Face ASSY | Fails to insulate — incorrect material choice | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×2 = 8 | Polycarbonate material choice / **RSK_R169** | 4×2 = 8 ✅ |
| DRSK0065 | E1 Emitter | MS-10268 Emitter Shell L | Enclosure damaged (large) — mechanical damage | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×3 = 12 | Compliance to IEC 60601-1 / **PRD20.5** | 4×3 = 12 ✅ |
| DRSK0068 | E1 Emitter | MS-10268 Emitter Shell L | Fails to maintain clearances | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×2 = 8 | Compliance to IEC 60601-1 / **PRD20.5** | 4×2 = 8 ✅ |
| DRSK0069 | E1 Emitter | MS-10268 Emitter Shell L | Fails to insulate | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×2 = 8 | Polycarbonate material choice / **RSK_R169** | 4×2 = 8 ✅ |
| DRSK0072 | E1 Emitter | MS-10134 Shell R Populated | Enclosure damaged (large) | **Minor Electrical Shock** | 4×3 = 12 | Compliance to IEC 60601-1 / **PRD20.5** | (same) ✅ |

All DFMEA electrical shock risks are rated Severity 4 (Minor — *"temporary injury not requiring professional medical intervention"*), indicating the MX1 is battery-powered and the maximum accessible voltage under single-fault conditions is bounded. All risks remained at or below Broadly Acceptable thresholds post-mitigation. <cite>RSK-P01-012 Rev C</cite>

---

## 3. Design Requirements Flowing from Risk Controls

The risk mitigations above flow into formal product requirements documented in the MX1 Design Inputs:

| Req ID | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **PRD20.5** | Device shall comply with IEC 60601-1 (General Safety — includes leakage current, dielectric strength, insulation clearances, creepage distances, and single-fault conditions) |
| **PRD20.6** | Power supply/charger shall comply with IEC 60601-1-2 §8.9 (Surge Protection) |
| **RSK_R118** | Over-voltage protection on battery charging circuit |
| **RSK_R361** | TVS Diodes and MOVs on USB power lines |
| **RSK_R169** | Impact and heat-resistant (polycarbonate) enclosure material to maintain insulation under mechanical damage |

<cite>DR-P01-005 Rev G</cite> <cite>RSK-P01-010 Rev E</cite>

---

## 4. Single-Fault Condition Analysis

A dedicated single-fault condition review was performed and is referenced in the Risk Management File. <cite>RSK-P01-017 Rev B</cite> The document **MEMO-P01-442** (Single Fault Conditions Determination) is cited as an input to the RMF. The 60601-1 compliance demonstrated by Intertek (see §5 below) inherently encompasses single-fault leakage current testing per IEC 60601-1 §8.7 and §8.8.

---

## 5. Verification Evidence — Electrical Safety & Leakage Testing

Two third-party test campaigns directly close the leakage-current risk loop:

### 5A. Primary IEC 60601-1 Safety Test (MX1 Rev E)

**Document:** `3P-P01-28` (Intertek; referenced throughout the V&V summary and trace matrix)
**Scope:** Full IEC 60601-1 type testing including:
- Earth leakage current (§8.7.3)
- Enclosure leakage current (§8.7.4)
- Patient leakage current (§8.7.5)
- Patient auxiliary leakage current (§8.7.6)
- Dielectric strength (§8.8)
- Single fault condition leakage (§8.7.3–8.7.6 under SFC)

**Standards verified:** IEC 60601-1:2005 Ed.3+A2:2020; IEC 60601-1-3; IEC 60601-1-6; IEC 60601-2-28; IEC 60601-2-54
**Result:** **PASS** <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>

### 5B. Supplemental Dielectric and Leakage Re-Test (MX1 Rev F — post C1 Cassette PCBA change)

**Document:** `3P-P01-33` (Intertek)
**Trigger:** A modification to the isolated DC/DC converter (the 5V power rail on the isolated USB port region of the C1 Cassette Main PCBA) was assessed in MEMO-P01-699 as requiring repeat 60601-1 dielectric and leakage testing.

Key details from the test report:
- **Scope:** E1 Emitter (SN1281), C1 Cassette (SN1280), H1 Wired Chargers (Lot 10146 ×2), F1 Foot Pedal (Lot 10045), K1 Cart (SN1203), Collimation Pucks (Lot 10148), T1 Tablet; SW v4.0.0-alpha
- **Test standard:** IEC 60601-1:2005 Ed.3+A1+A2
- **Test method:** USB-C adapter with shorted conductors to comply with IEC 60601-1 §8.8.3 (simulates worst-case applied part configuration for leakage measurement)
- **Result:** *"The MX1 Portable X-ray System Rev F passed all Dielectric and Leakage safety evaluations per IEC 60601-1."*
- **Conclusion:** *"The MX1 Portable X-ray System Rev F complies with the requirements indicated in IEC 60601-1:2005 Ed.3+A1+A2."*

<cite>3P-P01-33 Rev A</cite>

---

## 6. Traceability through the V&V Matrix

The V&V Trace Matrix (VVAM-P01-004 Rev D) contains a dedicated IEC 60601-1 sheet that maps every clause of IEC 60601-1 — including leakage current clauses under Section 8 — to its compliance method and documentary evidence. The Risk_Mitigations sheet links RSK risk IDs back to PRD requirements and verification reports. The summary report states:

> *"All mitigations specified by the Analysis were implemented. The mitigations were verified through the MX1 Verification and Validation activities. See VVAM-P01-004 - MX1 Verification & Validation Trace Matrix."*

<cite>RSK-P01-017 Rev B</cite> <cite>VVAM-P01-004 Rev D</cite>

The V&V Summary confirms Attachment **EM-03** (Electrical Safety) passed with report **3P-P01-28** for Rev E, and that **3P-P01-33** (Rev F targeted re-test) also passed: *"PASS — Electrical Safety Testing — IEC 60601-1: 2020-08 Ed. 3.2."* <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>

---

## 7. Full Traceability Chain (Summary Diagram)

```
HAZARD IDENTIFICATION
RSK-P01-010 Rev E (Hazard Analysis)
  └─ R0057: Peripheral insulation failure → electric shock / device damage
  └─ R0059: Over-voltage on USB → battery explosion risk
  └─ R0060: MAINS surge overcomes insulation
  └─ R0062: Incorrect outlet voltage overcomes insulation
RSK-P01-012 Rev C (DFMEA)
  └─ DRSK0042/0045/0046/0065/0068/0069/0072+: Enclosure damage / insulation failure → Minor Electrical Shock
         ↓
RISK CONTROLS (mitigations)
  ├─ PRD20.5  →  Full IEC 60601-1 compliance (leakage, dielectric, SFC, clearances)
  ├─ PRD20.6  →  IEC 60601-1-2 §8.9 surge protection on MAINS supply
  ├─ RSK_R118 →  Over-voltage protection on charging circuit
  ├─ RSK_R361 →  TVS Diodes + MOVs on USB power lines
  └─ RSK_R169 →  Polycarbonate enclosure (insulating, impact-resistant)
         ↓
DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
  DR-P01-005 Rev G (Design Inputs)
  └─ PRD20.5, PRD20.6, RSK_R118, RSK_R361, RSK_R169 formally captured
         ↓
V&V PLAN
  PLN-P01-065 Rev C
  └─ IEC 60601-1 type testing assigned to Intertek (3P test lab)
         ↓
VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
  ├─ 3P-P01-28 (Intertek, MX1 Rev E) → PASS — IEC 60601-1 full electrical safety
  │    including earth, enclosure, patient leakage current; dielectric; SFC
  └─ 3P-P01-33 (Intertek, MX1 Rev F) → PASS — Dielectric & Leakage re-test
         after C1 Cassette DC/DC converter isolation component change
         ↓
TRACE MATRIX & CLOSURE
  VVAM-P01-004 Rev D  →  IEC 60601-1 sheet maps every clause to evidence
  MEMO-P01-685 Rev A  →  V&V Summary confirms EM-03 PASS
  RSK-P01-017 Rev B   →  Risk Management Summary confirms all mitigations verified
                          "overall residual risk is acceptable"
```

---

## 8. Notable Observations

1. **All post-mitigation electrical shock risks are rated Severity 4 / Minor** — consistent with the MX1 being an internally-powered (battery) device with no mains-connected applied parts contacting the patient. The worst-case leakage path is via the USB-C charging port during charging, which is bounded by the required peripheral isolation and protection components. <cite>RSK-P01-010 Rev E</cite> <cite>RSK-P01-012 Rev C</cite>

2. **The Rev F re-test (3P-P01-33) was a targeted response to a specific hardware change** (C1 Cassette isolated DC/DC converter), triggered via a regulatory assessment (MEMO-P01-699) and risk-assessed in the V&V Plan. This is a positive indicator of the change control process functioning correctly. <cite>3P-P01-33 Rev A</cite>

3. **RSK-P01-010 Rev E is marked Obsolete**, though it is the latest revision. This is an administrative status flag in the document filename. The Risk Management Summary (RSK-P01-017 Rev B) references it as the current authoritative hazard analysis. <cite>RSK-P01-017 Rev B</cite>

4. **The DFMEA (RSK-P01-012 Rev C) is also flagged Obsolete** in the filename but is the latest revision (C), with the most recent update reflecting BOM-055 Rev H, I, J, & K changes. <cite>RSK-P01-012 Rev C</cite>

5. **No unmitigated risks** were identified in the electrical safety domain — the Risk Management Summary explicitly states: *"The MX1 System contains no unmitigated risks."* <cite>RSK-P01-017 Rev B</cite>

question: Does the Design History File provide enough evidence to support a complete design-control coverage claim?
answer:
I now have a thorough picture of the DHF. Let me compile the full analysis.

---

## DHF Design-Control Coverage Assessment: MX1 Portable X-ray System

Based on a comprehensive review of **DHF-008 Rev D** (the DHF Checklist), **MEMO-P01-685 Rev A** (V&V Summary), **VVAM-P01-004 Rev D** (V&V Trace Matrix), **RSK-P01-017 Rev B** (Risk Management Report), and the Phase 3 and Phase 4 Closure Records, the DHF is **substantively strong and broadly supports a complete design-control coverage claim**, but carries **several documented open items and caveats** that are important to understand. Here is a structured assessment:

---

## ✅ What Is Well-Covered

### 1. Design Planning (Phase 1)
All planning deliverables are fully populated with released documents:
- Project plan, project schedule, IP review, quality plan, regulatory plan, software development plan, cybersecurity plan, usability plan, and risk management plan are all referenced and released. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>
- The DHF checklist itself was established at Phase 1 and audited by QA (Eden Jameson, 15 Mar 2024). <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>

### 2. Design Inputs (Phase 2)
- Design inputs are captured in <cite>DR-P01-005 Rev G</cite>, with use cases in <cite>MEMO-P01-412 Rev B</cite>, use specification in <cite>MEMO-P01-642 Rev D</cite>, and user interface specification in <cite>MEMO-P01-655 Rev C</cite>.
- Initial hazard analyses (device, software, cybersecurity, DFMEA) are all referenced to <cite>RSK-P01-010</cite> and <cite>RSK-P01-011</cite>.
- Software specifications (SRS, SDS, SAD, Software BOM, SOUP, etc.) are fully documented across multiple memo documents and BOMs. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>
- The V&V Trace Matrix was established at Phase 2. <cite>VVAM-P01-004 Rev D</cite>

### 3. Design Verification (Phase 3)
This is the most heavily populated section. Evidence includes:
- **EMC/EMI, electrical safety, wireless coexistence**: Tested per IEC 60601-1, -1-2, -1-3, -1-6, -2-28, -2-43, -2-54 by SGS (3P-P01-26, 3P-P01-32) and Intertek (3P-P01-28, 3P-P01-33) — all **PASS**. <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>
- **Radiation performance** (focal spot, HVL, residual radiation, output reproducibility, linearity/constancy, dosimetric indications): All separately verified via dedicated VVPR reports. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>
- **Physical/mechanical specs** (weight, battery life, foot pedal distance, cleaning durability, collimation, SSD/SID accuracy, WTX FOD): Each with a dedicated VVPR. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>
- **Software verification**: Exhaustive — 9 SW version lines (v3.0.0 through v4.1.0) each with their own dedicated VVPRs covering system configuration, power states, technique factors, safety interlocks, radiographic/radioscopic acquisition, foot pedal integration, charging, device app, critical faults, voltage/temperature monitoring, motion interlock, viewfinder UI, beam angle, SSD, penetration testing, fuzz testing, code reviews, and cloud service provider inspections. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite> <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>
- **Summative usability evaluation** completed (<cite>VVPR-P01-081 Rev B</cite>), along with two formative evaluations. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>
- **Image quality study** (<cite>VVPR-P01-187 Rev B</cite>) and DICOM display testing completed.
- **Biocompatibility assessment**: <cite>MEMO-P01-674 Rev D</cite>
- **Packaging V&V**: ISTA 3A — **PASS**. <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>
- **Battery testing**: UN38.3 and IEC 62133-2 — **PASS**. <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite>
- **Final V&V Trace Matrix** cross-references all inputs (PRD, risk, usability, standards) to compliance methods and results. <cite>VVAM-P01-004 Rev D</cite>

### 4. Risk Management
- Full risk management file assembled including hazard analysis (<cite>RSK-P01-010</cite>), DFMEA (<cite>RSK-P01-012 Rev C</cite>), URRA (<cite>RSK-P01-013 Rev C</cite>), Security Risk Assessment (<cite>RSK-P01-011 Rev C</cite>), MedAI PFMEA (<cite>RSK-P01-016 Rev A</cite>), F1 Foot Pedal PFMEA (<cite>RSK-P01-020 Rev A</cite>), and CMO PFMEAs (555-0015, -0016, -0018).
- Risk Management Summary Report states: **"The MX1 System contains no unmitigated risks"** and overall residual risk is deemed acceptable. <cite>RSK-P01-017 Rev B</cite>
- All risk mitigations were verified through V&V activities cross-referenced to <cite>VVAM-P01-004 Rev D</cite>.

### 5. Design Transfer (Phase 4)
- Design transfer plan, DHRs, assembly work instructions, process validation master plans, non-product software validations, and workstation IQ/OQ records are all present. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>
- 510(k) clearance K241567 received Dec 6, 2024. <cite>MEMO-P01-859 Rev A</cite>
- Phase 4 DHF audit completed by QA (Cameron Rivera, 23 Mar 2025); Director of QA/RA approval for commercial release signed 24 Mar 2025. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>

---

## ⚠️ Documented Gaps and Open Items

### 1. Process Qualification (PQ) Reports Not Finalized at Phase 4 Closure
The Phase 4 Closure Record records the following as incomplete:
- **F1 Foot Pedal PQ Report**: "complete with passing results. Report to be finalized and released in Phase 5."
- **Sanmina Emitter and MX1 PQ Reports**: "complete with passing results. Reports to be finalized and released in Phase 5."

Phase 4 was closed by executive authorization before these reports were formally released. Sanmina also identified yield improvement needs. <cite>MEMO-P01-859 Rev A</cite>

### 2. WS-002 and WS-006 IQ/OQ Not Completed at Sanmina
Phase 4 meeting minutes note that "IQ/OQ has not been completed for WS-002 and WS-006" at Sanmina, though MedAI's equivalents were completed. <cite>MEMO-P01-859 Rev A</cite>

### 3. Several Phase 2 DHF Deliverables Marked Blank (No Document Reference)
Three items in the Phase 2 checklist have no document referenced:
- **EU MDR Classification Document** — blank, annotated "Required for CE Marking only"
- **Hazardous Substances BOM Review (RoHS/REACH)** — blank
- **International Trade Compliance Review (ITAR/EAR)** — blank
<cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>

Similarly in Phase 3:
- **Stability/Shelf Life Protocols and Reports** — blank
- **Clinical Evaluation Plan** — blank
- **Clinical Evaluation Report** — blank
- **Hazardous Substances Assessment (RoHS/REACH/WEEE)** — blank
- **Test Method Validation** — blank (Phase 4)
- **Postmarket Surveillance Plan** — blank (Phase 4)
- **Post Market Clinical Follow Up Plan** — blank (Phase 4)
- **Final GSPRs / Canada Safety / Australia Essential Principles** — blank (Phase 4)
<cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>

> **Note**: The footnote in DHF-008 Rev D clarifies that items marked * (CE Marking), ** (Canada), and *** (Australia) are not required for US market distribution. The product has been cleared for US distribution via 510(k), so these are not necessarily coverage gaps for the current clearance scope.

### 4. Device Master Record (DMR) Index for CMO Not Yet Provided
- DMR for CMO (Sanmina-produced MX1) is noted as "Index to be provided in Phase 5." <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>

### 5. VVPR-P01-205 Listed in DHF but Not Found in Corpus
The DHF references **VVPR-P01-205** (MX1 Usability Summative Evaluation) in the Phase 3 checklist under "Summative Usability Evaluation," but the corpus only contains **VVPR-P01-081** (which holds the same title). This could be a document numbering inconsistency worth clarifying. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite>

### 6. Software Anomalies Pending Resolution
- <cite>MEMO-P01-685 Rev A</cite> notes that anomalies in **MEMO-P01-826** (MX1 SW v4.1.0 Unresolved Anomalies) "shall be addressed and verified prior to future release" and will be "risk assessed to determine acceptability prior to launch." MEMO-P01-826 is not itself in the current corpus, though this is expected as it is flagged as a pending action.

---

## 🔵 Overall Verdict

| Design Control Element | Coverage Status |
|---|---|
| Design Planning | ✅ Complete |
| Design Inputs | ✅ Complete |
| Design Outputs (specs, BOMs, drawings) | ✅ Complete (drawings referenced by pointer) |
| Design Reviews (Phases 1–4) | ✅ Complete with signatures |
| Design Verification | ✅ Extensive (hardware, software, third-party) |
| Design Validation (usability, clinical) | ✅ Summative complete; clinical eval deferred (US-only scope) |
| Risk Management | ✅ Full ISO 14971 compliance claimed |
| V&V Traceability | ✅ VVAM-P01-004 traces inputs to results |
| Design Transfer | ✅ Mostly complete; PQ reports pending Phase 5 finalization |
| Postmarket Surveillance | ⚠️ Plan not yet documented in DHF |

**The DHF provides strong evidence for a complete design-control coverage claim for US 510(k) purposes.** The checklist spans four formal phases, each closed with QA audit signatures, and the V&V corpus is exceptionally deep (50+ VVPRs plus third-party reports). The documented open items (PQ report finalization, some Sanmina workstation qualifications, CMO DMR index) are consistent with a Phase 4/Phase 5 transition and are acknowledged in the closure records — they do not invalidate the core design control chain.

The main areas requiring attention for completeness in broader market claims (EU, Canada, Australia) and for post-market phase entry are the regulatory-region-specific documents and the postmarket surveillance plan, none of which have been entered into the DHF yet. <cite>DHF-008 Rev D</cite> <cite>MEMO-P01-859 Rev A</cite>
